findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are embedded in plaintext within the instance user_data script, which is visible via the EC2 metadata service and Terraform state, risking credential theft.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and exposed if the underlying storage is compromised.
The EBS snapshot inherits encryption settings from the unencrypted source volume, so the snapshot data is also stored unencrypted, exposing it to unauthorized access if leaked or shared.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and unauthorized access attempts from any IP address on the internet.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0, which combined with unrestricted egress, expands the attack surface unnecessarily for a web-facing host without any additional protections.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used for VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block, potentially allowing unencrypted storage and public exposure of sensitive network flow log data.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to the internet for resources that may not need direct public access.
